On this day, in the year 163 of the martyrs (447 A.D.), the Holy Father St. Arsenius—tutor of the imperial children—departed in peace. He was born in Rome in 350 A.D. to wealthy and devout parents, who raised him in the teachings of the Church. He was ordained a deacon and mastered both Greek and Latin, excelling in them. His reputation for virtue and learning reached Emperor Theodosius the Great, who summoned Arsenius to instruct his two sons, Honorius and Arcadius. The young princes loved and respected him greatly.

Yet St. Arsenius was continually mindful of the vanity of the world. He often prayed, “Lord, guide me in the way of salvation.” One day he heard a divine voice saying, “Flee from people, and you shall be saved.” Obedient to this call, he took his sister to Constantinople and entrusted her to a convent of one hundred and twenty nuns. He then departed for Alexandria and from there journeyed to the wilderness of Shiheet (Scetis). He became first a disciple of St. John (Yehness) Colobos (The Short), and later of St. Isaiah the Elder (Al-Eskeety). He strove with great diligence in asceticism, fasting, prayer, and long night vigils. After three years, he again heard a voice saying, “Keep your serenity, withdraw from people, and be silent, and you will be saved.” He then secluded himself in a cave away from the monastery.

Once, seeking counsel about his thoughts, he spoke with one of the elders. A fellow monk overheard and asked him, “Does Arsenius—learned in Greek and Roman culture—seek advice from this uneducated Egyptian?” Arsenius replied, “In Greek and Roman knowledge I am well trained, but in the alphabet, in which this simple monk excels, I have not yet learned.” By this he meant the monk’s spiritual wisdom and moral excellence.

St. Arsenius frequently reminded himself, “O Arsenius, remember the purpose for which you left the world.” Thus he spent many nights in tears, weeping so much that the hairs of his eyelashes fell out.

Once the most finely dressed man in the imperial court, he became after his monastic vow the least concerned with appearances. He ate sparingly, labored with his hands, and when he attended church, he always stood hidden behind a particular pillar.

When Pope Theophilus, the 23rd Patriarch, wished to visit him, he sent a messenger ahead. The saint replied, “Tell the Pope: ‘If you come, I will open my door to you. But if I open it for you, I will no longer be able to close it to anyone. And if I open my door to everyone, I cannot remain here.’” St. Arsenius excelled in the virtue of silence for which he is remembered for his famous saying: “I have often repented of having spoken, but never of having been silent.”

St. Arsenius witnessed the first Berber raid on the wilderness of Shiheet in 407 A.D. In 411 A.D. he went to Canopus, soon after he returned to Scetis, where he remained until 432 A.D. Because of further raids, he left the desert and took refuge in a monastery on Mount Torah—later known as the Monastery of El-Kosair or the Monastery of Heraclius—Also known as the Monastery of the mule-where he lived for ten years. In 442 A.D. he was again forced to leave due to Berber incursions and went to Canopus for three years, then returned once more to Mount Torah. There he spent his final two years and departed in peace in 447 A.D.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-13.title: The Departure of St. Arsenius, the Tutor of the Emperor's Children

09-13.html:
On this day also of the year 21 of the martyrs (305 A.D.) the Saint Abba Pigol (Begoul) the Soldier, was martyred. This saint was born in the city of Tala, el-Minya governorate to godly parents and he was inclined since his young age to a life of chastity.

When he enlisted in the army, he spent his salary on the poor and the needy. He persevered on the life of vigils, praises, continuous fasting and prayers, serving the infirm and the prisoners.

The saint left the army and went to the wilderness which was west of Tala to dedicate his life to prayers and worship. He went every Saturday to the nearby church, spent the night in praising God then partook of the holy mysteries by the hand of St. Pigol.

The angel of the Lord appeared to him, strengthened and encouraged the saint and told him that he would be martyred. He went to Alexandria and declared his faith before Armanius the governor. He ordered to scourge him until his bones were exposed. The Lord sent his angel who healed him. The governor became angry so he placed him on an iron bed and lit fire under but the fire became like cold dew. When the governor became weary of tormenting him, he sent him to Arianus, governor of Ansena, who tortured him with the Hinbazeen. His face was shining and his body was filled with strength. When Arianus saw that he cried out saying; “I will see who can save you from my hand.” He ordered to pull out the nails of his hands and legs, to beat him with an iron spout, to hang him on a tall mast, head down, then cut the rope so he would fall on his head and die however the angel of the Lord saved him. Many of the people of Ansena believed.

Arianus sent him to Emperor Diocletian in Antioch where he again confessed the Lord Christ before him. He ordered to imprison him where he was visited by St. Victor Ebn Romanus. Many miracles took place in prison which enraged the emperor. He ordered to cast him in a dark pit and to cover it with a heavy rock to die therein. The next morning the soldier found his arms spread out praying so the emperor ordered him beheaded thus he received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-13.title: The Martyrdom of the Saint Abba Pigol (Begoul) the Soldier

09-14.html:
On this day of the year 64 of the martyrs (348 A.D.), Abba Pachomius, the father of the spiritual monastic communal life (Cenobitic life), departed. This Holy Father was born in Thebes (Luxor) to pagan parents about the year 290 A.D. He loved since his young age the life of purity and chastity. He rejected pagan worship and refused to participate in its feasts. His father once took him to offer a sacrifice to the devils which were in the river. When a pagan priest saw him, shouted out saying; “Keep away the enemy of the gods from here so they would cease their anger from us.”

He was recruited in the Roman army. On his way with several other youth to subdue a revolt against the emperor by the king of Ethiopia, they rested at the shore of the city of Latopolis (Esna). Its people came out and offered them food and drink generously with joy. Pachomius asked about the reason of their kindness. He was told that they do this for the sake of the God of heaven. He decided to become a Christian if he returned safely. With divine providence the revolt was abated and the soldiers were discharged.

The saint went to Dandara where he registered his name in the catechumen’s list. Then he was baptized by the hand of Anba Serapion bishop of Dandara in the year 314 A.D. He remained about three years performing deeds of charity and mercy and his heart was inflamed with the desire of consecration. He went to the saint Anba Balamon (Palaemon) where he became a monk and stayed for seven years in obedience and submission to him. He mastered well the ways of the monastic life.

Then the angel of the Lord appeared to him and commanded him to establish the system of the monastic communal life. He told his teacher Anba Balamon about the command of the angel. He was exceedingly happy, blessed the project and went with him to Tabennesi. He aided Abba Pachomius in establishing the first monastery. Then he bid him farewell to return to his cave with the agreement to meet once a year.

Soon after, many joined the communal monasticism so St. Pachomius built for them ten monasteries. His older brother John came, became a monk under his guidance and assisted him in establishing the monasteries. His sister also came to him; he encouraged her on the monastic life, and built for her a convent east of the Nile that housed about three hundred nuns.

He had all the monasteries under one system of manual labor, certain times for communal prayers and as of fasting, the monk ate twice a day. He was the father of all the monasteries and appointed an Abbot in each monastery. He visited the monasteries and their monks regularly to oversee their affairs. Anba Pachomius refused the priestly ranks in the monasteries. When Pope Athanasius wanted to ordain him a priest, he fled away from him. The Pope told his children the monks; “Tell your father, he who built his house on the rock that can’t be shaken, and fled from the vainglory of the world, is blessed, and his disciples are also blessed.” When he was assured that the Pope will not ordain him, he received him on his way back from Aswan with great joy.

The saint opened the doors of the cenobitic monasteries to the non-Egyptian from the Greeks, Romans and others and each of these groups had a leader over it. He allowed the solitary life for those who desired it.

The saint was known for his meekness and humility. One of the brethren asked him to describe for him one of the spiritual visions and he replied saying; “If you see a meek and humble brother do not seek any other sight. The saint loved his children but he was also firm.

He remained the father of the Cenobitic monasteries until the spread of Plague in Egypt. The saint went around the ill monks with plague to minister unto them. While he was attending the prayers of the feast of Ascension he felt the signs of this evil illness in his body. After the end of the service he called his disciples and appointed for them St. Petronius to be the head of the monasteries after him, then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-14.title: The Departure of St. Pachomius (Pakhom), the Father of the Spiritual Communal Monastic life (Cenobitic life)

09-14.html:
On this day also of the year 250 A.D. St. Epimachus of Pelusium was martyred. He was born in Farma (Pelusium) and he worked as a weaver. He was gentle, quiet and loving the life of contemplation. He often went to the wilderness nearby el-Farma longing for the life of asceticism and worship however he received the crown of martyrdom instead of this angelic life.

When he heard about the horrific torment that the Christian suffered in Alexandria, he decided to go to meet the governor. He travelled to Alexandria and went to the courtyard with his peasant clothes, knocking down a pagan altar of incense and admonished the magistrate for his savagery. The soldiers jumped over him, scourged him, chained the saint with fetters and cast him in prison. He comforted the confessors and encouraged them to be steadfast in the faith which exasperated the magistrate more. When he came before the court he confessed the Lord Christ. The ruler ordered to hang him naked and scourged until his flesh was torn. Then he ordered him be squeezed by the Hinbazeen, he bled and a drop of his blood fell on the eyes of a blind child and she received her sight. Her family believed in the Lord Christ and received the crown of martyrdom. That enraged the governor who ordered to behead the saint. When the executioner drew his sword all power left him and he was unable to strike, and so with fourteen other executioners who all tried to behead St. Epimachus. When they failed to behead him, tied a rope around his neck and was dragged until he delivered his spirit in the hand of the Lord and received the crown of martyrdom.

A deaf person carried his body to cast it away, when he touched the body his ears were opened and was able to hear. Some believers from Edko came, took the body and shrouded it. A church was built after his name in el-Farma to which the body was relocated.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-14.title: The Martyrdom of St. Epimachus (Ephimachus) of Pelusium

09-15.html:
On this day of the year 68 A.D. St. Simon the Zealot, one of the twelve apostles, was martyred. He was born in Cana of Galilee and was called the Zelotes for he was a member of the revolting Zealotes movement. They had a fervent zeal for the Mosaic Law. He was associated with them for about twenty years before the Lord called him.

Simon the Canaanite (the Zealot) was the one whom the Lord Christ attended his wedding at Cana of Galilee and turned the water into wine. He was touched by the Lord Christ who called him for the ministry and he left everything and followed Him. He witnessed the feeding of the multitudes from the five loaves and two fish. This saint is depicted in the icons of the Greek Church carrying a fishing rod with a fish or carrying a basket of bread.

After receiving the grace of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost went to North Africa (Carthage) and from there he traveled to Spain. Then he preached in the British Isles along with St. Joseph of Arimathea and established a church for them then returned to Palestine.

Afterwards he accompanied the apostle St. Judas (Thaddeus) and preached together in Syria, Mesopotamia (Iraq) then went to Persia. There they found an army ready to invade India. When they entered the camp, the devils who were prophesying through the magician became silent. They spoke from one of the idols saying; “This had happened because of the presence of Judas and Simon the apostles of Christ.” The Commander of the camp wanted to listen to them. They preached to him the Lord Christ, His salvation, omnipotence, and His authority. Then they told him; “Tomorrow messengers from India will come carrying a truce and it is in your favor.” When the prophecy was fulfilled, the two apostles gained favor in the sight of the commander and his soldiers. They believed in the Lord Christ and a multitude of people believed also.

Then they went around preaching the Gospel until they came to the city of Shinar. The priests of the idols and the diviners stirred up the rulers and the people against the apostles. They seized and cast them in prison. When they commanded them to worship the sun and the stars they confessed their faith in the Lord Christ openly and with complete courage. They jumped over the two apostles killing them. They slew Judas with an ax and spear and Simon was sawn with a saw thus they received the crowns of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-15.title: The Martyrdom of St. Simon the Zealot (Simon the Canaanite), one of the Twelve Apostles

09-15.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) four hundred persons were martyred in Dandara. They witnessed the torment of St. Babnuda (Paphnute), the hermit, at the hands of Arianus, governor of Ansena, in the city of Dandara. When they saw his miracles, they believed in the Lord Christ and declared their faith before the governor who burnt them thus they received the crowns of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-15.title: The Martyrdom of 400 martyrs in Dandara (Denderah)

09-15.html:
On this day also the church celebrates the commemoration of the martyrdom of Deacon Mina the anchorite.

The blessing of his prayer be with us all. Amen.
09-15.title: The Martyrdom of the Hermit St. Mina the Deacon

09-15.html:
Today also of the year 1040 of the martyrs (1324 A.D.) marks the departure of the priest Al-Mo’ataman Shams El-Ri'asah Abi El-Barakat known as Ebn Kabr. His father was wealthy so he received a good deal of education which qualified him to join the career of the government’s scribes. He was promoted in the ranks until he took the position of the scribe of prince Baybars. He served him with sincerity and complete honesty.

When king el-Ashraf reigned he expelled all the Christians from their positions in the government and from serving the princes. Abu el-Barakat resigned and dedicated himself to study the religious, theological and historical subjects. In the year 1300 A.D. he was ordained a priest for the Virgin St. Mary church, el-Mu’allaqah, in Old Cairo. He continued his learning of the books of the fathers and it did help him being close to the contemporary Popes for the patriarchal place at that time was in el-Mu’allaqah church.

He wrote a group of beneficial books as the book;”The lamp of darkness to clarify the rituals,” and another book describing the materials used in making the holy Myron and the way of cooking it. He also gathered in one book many of the church canons. In the later part of his life he dedicated himself to writing and reviewing his comprehensive works. He suffered severe weakness and delivered up his pure spirit.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-15.title: The Departure of the Priest Shams El-Ri'asah Abi El-Barakat known as Ebn Kabr

09-16.html:
On this day the church commemorates the consecration of the church of St. John the Evangelist in the city of Alexandria. St. John was the brother of St. James the Elder who were the sons of Zebedee.

He preached the Gospel in Asia Minor, established the seven churches mentioned in the book of Revelation, wrote the gospel attributed to him, three epistles and the book of Revelation.

The church called him the apostle of love for his epistles overflow with love. In his old age, he was carried to the church at Ephesus, and his sole exhortation was, “Little children, love one another.”

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-16.title: The Consecration of the church of St. John the Evangelist in the city of Alexandria

09-17.html:
On this day of the year 119 of the martyrs (403 A.D.) the great father St. Epiphanius, bishop of Cyprus, departed. He was born about the year 307 A.D. to Jewish parents in Palestine. His father died, left a great wealth and left him and his sister and their mother brought them up well.

Once, when he was walking in the road, he saw a poor man asking for alms and he did not pay attention to him. He asked one of the monks, and the monk took off his garment and gave it to him since he did not have anything else to give him. St. Epiphanius saw a white dress coming down from heaven upon the monk instead of the garment that he gave away. Epiphanius marveled and went to the monk and asked him about his faith. The monk told him that he was Christian. He asked the monk to guide him to the facts of this religion. The monk brought him to the bishop of the region who taught and exhorted him then baptized him.

Epiphanius desired the monastic life, so the bishop sent him to the monastery of St. Lucianus. He became a disciple to St. Hilarion who prophesied that he would be a bishop. He learned Hebrew, Coptic, Syrian, Greek, and Latin and also studied the Holy Bible. St. Jerome called him, “He who has five tongues.”

Because he loved the life of asceticism and contemplation, he left Palestine and went to Egypt about the year 335 A.D. where he met a group of hermits and monks before his seclusion in a monastery in Alexandria.

Some Gnostics felt his abilities, gifts and desires and wanted to recruit him. They sent to him some adulterous women to entice him but with the grace of God he did not fall into sin. For this reason he dedicated a great deal of his power to refute the heretics.

He established a monastery in Palestine and he was very stern with himself. One of his disciples asked him, how could he endure this asceticism that exceeds his strength? He replied; “God does not grant us the kingdom unless we struggle, and all what we endure does not compare to the crown that we are struggling for.”

The bishop of the city realized the effort of St. Epiphanius among his people who gathered around him seeking his advice and blessings. He ordained him a priest to make more use of his talents. Meanwhile, St. Hilarion left the area for multitudes of people gathered around him and went to Cyprus. The bishops, priests and the people came to receive his blessing. He talked to them about St. Epiphanius, his asceticism, virtues, knowledge and his zeal. When the bishop of the city of Salamis on the island of Cyprus reposed, they chose him a bishop for it, against his will, in the year 367 A.D.

St. Epiphanius was distinguished with his ardent zeal and firmness toward the Orthodox faith with great love for the poor. He used to give whatever he had in the Episcopal place; however God sent to him much more to give to the poor. The widow St. Olympias granted him endowments for that purpose. His love for the poor was the main reason for him accepting the Christian faith as we had seen earlier. Once his disciple asked him to put a limit to the giving since there was nothing left. Right after this conversation a stranger came and gave the bishop a sack of gold and immediately disappeared. In his biography it was mentioned that a deceiver came to ask for alms to bury his friend and he gave him. When he returned to his friend he found him in fact dead.

St. Epiphanius departed when he was about ninety six years old.

He had many sayings on asceticism and morality, to mention a few:

(1) Reading the Holy Bible is a great security against sin and the ignorance of the Holy Scriptures is a bottomless pit and a great gulf.

(2) Do not love the things of the world, you will have rest and joy at the last day. Keep away from the pleasures of the world so you will not be overcome with the grief of the devils.

(3) Keep your heart alert by mentioning God and that will ease the attacks of the enemy against you.

(4) God sells righteousness very cheap for those who want to buy: with a small piece of bread, humble clothes, a cup of cold water or one mite.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-17.title: The Departure of St. Epiphanius, Bishop of Cyprus

09-18.html:
This day marks the commemoration of the coming down of the Holy Spirit upon the holy disciples in the upper room of Zion in Jerusalem. “When the day of Pentecost had fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven, as of a rushing mighty wind, and filled the whole house where they were sitting. Then there appeared to them divided tongues, as of fire, and one sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit.”

The blessing of this holy feast be with us all. Amen.
09-18.title: The Commemoration of the feast of Pentecost

09-18.html:
On this day also of the year 409 of the martyrs (693 A.D.) St. George (Ga'orgi), who was the friend of St. Abraam, departed. He was born to godly Christian parents, and he tended the sheep of his father. He loved the life of contemplation and seclusion and he fasted all daylong and distributed his food among the shepherds. God supported and increased him in godliness.

He longed for the monastic life, so he left the tending of the sheep. He was fourteen years old when he went to the wilderness of St. Macarius. On his way he saw a pillar of light guiding him so he rejoiced and was comforted. The light disappeared and the devil appeared to him in the form of an old man who said to him: "Your father thought that a lion had killed you while tending to the sheep, and he rent his garment and grieved over you. Now it is meet that you should return to your father to comfort his heart first for it is written; “Honor your father and mother” then return to the wilderness." The young man replied saying it is written: “He who loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me." Immediately that old man became like smoke and disappeared. George realized that it was a devilish deception and he offered thanks to God.

Immediately, Archangel Gabriel appeared to him in the form of a young man who guided him to the mountain of Abba Orion (Arion) nearby Shiheet (Scetis). He remained there under the guidance of a holy monk for ten years, during which he did not eat any cooked food or fruits. He kept long vigils in prayers and contemplation in the Holy Scripture until he memorized fourteen books of the Holy Bible. Because of his austere asceticism he was worthy of the company of angelic power to comfort and encourage him.

Then he desired to live in seclusion so he went to the inner wilderness. Two saints appeared to him and told him; “This is not the will of God for you,” accordingly he returned to his place. With God’s providence the Holy Father Anba Abraam came to the mountain of St. Orion where he met St. George (Ga'orgi). They conversed with each other about the wonders of God and they felt a spiritual closeness in their lives and wishes. They decided to live together to support each other. They went to the church to pray and spent all night seeking the Divine Providence for their decision. It was said that St. John the Baptist appeared to them and commanded them to dwell together in the Scetis of St. Macarius

St. Ga’orgi received the blessings of the fathers, left the mount of St. Orion and went to Shiheet. Anba Abraam had left before him to prepare a place for him. Anba Abraam introduced St. George to his teacher the Holy Father Anba Yoannis, the hegumen of the wilderness of Shiheet. They dwelt together in the cell known as Bigeeg beside the cell of Anba Yoannis.

This cell remained one of the sights of the monastery until the fourteenth century when Pope Benjamin II, 82nd Patriarch (1327-1339 A.D.) had visited this cell.

They lived together with the spirit of friendship encouraging each other. Later on Anba Abraam became ill for eighteen years during which he suffered from the severe pain. St. George served, prayed for him and read to him the Holy Scriptures until he departed in peace. Shortly after less than five months his brother St. George departed. He was seventy two years old and was buried beside his beloved brother Anba Abraam.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-18.title: The Departure of St. George (Ga'orgi), the Friend of St. Abraam

09-19.html:
On this day the Holy Father Abba Isaac, the priest of El-Qalali (Kellia-Cells), departed. He was born in Upper Egypt around the year 350 A.D. In his early childhood he used to visit the saint Anba Antonius. He was greatly influenced by his monastic life. He visited often in his youth “Baspeer” monastery. He was discipled at the hands of St. Macarius the abbot of the monastery.

In the year 370 A.D. he became a monk in Nitria and dwelt with his teacher Cronius whom he succeeded as the priest of Cellia (El-Qalali) in the year 395 A.D. Palladius told us that St. Isaac was the abbot of two hundred and ten monks. He built a hostel for the sojourners in the area of Cellia for the travelers to rest. St. Isaac lived in his asceticism for 30 years. He was one of the eight elders’ council who presided over Cellia and Nitria.

He was present during the visit of Pope Theophilus to Nitria to investigate the issue of the tall brothers. He was expelled from Nitria, as many others, to Palestine around the year 400 A.D. along with his namesake Fr. Isaac the priest of Shiheet. He returned about the year 403 A.D. from Palestine to Nitria.

In the later part of his days, he became ill of a grievous sickness that prevented him from performing his duties. Some of the brethren brought him cooked food but he refused to eat saying; “Believe me I would be content and thankful if I remained in my sickness for thirty years.” To this saint was the credit of conveying the teachings of the Holy Father Anba Pemwah to the monks of Cellia. He was very stern about the modesty of the monk’s attire.

The devil appeared to him once looking from the window of his cell and told him you had become from our followers. When he closely examined himself he remembered that he partook of the holy mysteries three consecutive Sundays while he was not in peace with one of the brethren. Immediately he rose in haste and asked the forgiveness of this brother with tears and supplication.

This saint witnessed the first raid of the Berbers on the wilderness in the year 407 A.D. At the time of his departure he told his disciples; "Strive to do exactly as you have seen me do and God is able to protect and keep you", then he departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayer be with us all. Amen.
09-19.title: The Departure of Abba Isaac, the Priest of El-Qalali (Cells)

09-19.html:
This day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) marks the martyrdom of St. Isidore of Antioch. He was born in Antioch and his father's name was Bandilaous (Bandla’on), who was one of the noble men in the empire of Diocletian. He was the governor of the city of Antioch. His mother's name was Sophia and he had a sister whose name was Euphemia.

When Diocletian apostatized, St. Bandla’on and his son Isidore left their home and went secretly to a mountain where they dwelt with a holy man whose name was Abba Samuel.

When the Emperor knew of what they had done, he brought them and asked for the reason of their fleeing to the mountain. They answered saying; “When you were worshipping the living God we loved, honored and served you. However when you forsook the worship of God and worshipped the idols we also abandoned you.” The emperor befriended St. Bandilaous to persuade him to deny the Lord Christ. When he did not obey him, he ordered him beheaded thus he received the crown of martyrdom.

The emperor imprisoned the young man Isidore and tortured him. When his mother heard that her son being tortured, she went with her daughter to comfort and strengthen him. She rebuked the emperor who ordered to behead them thus they received the crowns of martyrdom.

They tormented Isidore with the Hinbazeen, placed lit torches to his sides, laid him on an iron bed and lit fire under him. Then they cast him into the lions’ den which did not harm him and in all these hardships the Lord raised him well and His Holy Name was glorified.

The emperor exiled him to Seleucia where its governor Andronicus and his family believed at his hands. When the emperor was informed he summoned them all. He beheaded Andronicus and his entire family and threw the young man Isidore into a repulsive smelling prison without food or water to die. However the Lord sent His angel to offer him food and drink.

The emperor brought him and asked him to go with him to the temple and Isidore accepted. The emperor rejoiced, gathered his comrades and multitudes of people. In the temple the saint instead of kneeling to the idols he prayed to the Lord for the earth to swallow these idols. The emperor became exceedingly angry and ordered to nail the saint on a wooden cross until he delivered his pure spirit and received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-19.title: The Martyrdom of St. Isidorus (Isidore) of Antioch

09-20.html:
On this day of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) the six soldiers who accompanied St. Claudius, Stratelates, the martyr from Antioch to Egypt, were martyred. When Emperor Diocletian sent St. Claudius to Egypt to be tortured, Dioscorus, Dionysius, Phoebammon, Karus, Paphadius and Ammonius the soldiers accompanied him.

During the journey St. Claudius talked to them about the Lord Christ and the eternal life that He grants to the believers who are holding fast to Him, and they believed in the Lord Christ.

When they arrived to Arianus the governor they declared their faith in the Lord Christ. The governor marveled and ordered them beheaded. St. Claudius encouraged them until they received the crowns of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-20.title: The Martyrdom of the Six Soldiers who accompanied Claudius Stratelates, the Martyr

09-20.html:
On this day also, of the year 73 of the martyrs (357 A.D.), the Holy Father Abba Ammonius, the hermit on Mount Tounah, departed. He was born in the year 294 A.D. in Upper Egypt.

In his youth he saw in a vision St. Antonius calling him to the monastic life and guided him to an ascetic father called Anba Isidore. He went to St. Isidore, who put on him the holy Eskeem. He dwelt with him under his guidance until his teacher departed from this world.

St. Ammonius went to St. Antonius and was discipled at his hands. He dwelt in a cave nearby him. He struggled in worship and asceticism and the devil envied him. He came to him in the form of a woman and when he asked her to pray with him immediately the devil turned to smoke and fled away.

Abba Apollo, who was like the angels, wished to visit Anba Ammonius, he took with him Abba Yousab. After they had talked about the greatness of God, he asked him for a little of bread. He told them; “I do not have bread in my cell for I eat the herbs and the weeds of the wilderness.” They marveled at his worship and asceticism. During their prayers the angel of the Lord brought hot bread for them. After the prayer, they ate, thanked the Lord then bid him farewell and returned to their monastery.

The angel of the Lord appeared to St. Ammonius and informed him that he was about to depart. When he finished his good demeanor departed to the Lord whom he loved.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-20.title: The Departure of St. Ammonius the Hermit

09-21.html:
On this day, the church celebrates the monthly commemoration of the Mother of God the pure Virgin St. Mary, from whom was the salvation of the world.

Her holy intercession be with us all. Amen.
09-21.title: The Commemoration of the Holy and Pure Virgin St. Mary

09-21.html:
On this day also of the later part of the fourth century St. Marcian (Martinianus) departed. He was born in the city of Caesarea, Palestine. He became a monk under the guidance of a holy man living on mount el-Safina (The ship). He fought a great and strenuous fight with many ascetic worships.

An evil woman heard of him, and she wanted to entice him to fall in sin with her. She put on ragged clothes and waited until the evening, then knocked on the door of his cell, weeping, pretending that she had lost her way. She asked him to let her stay with him until the morning. After much insistence he allowed her in and placed her in a secluded place of the cell. In the morning he went to her to dismiss her but he found that she had adorned and perfumed herself. She started tempting him to commit sin with her. He went outside the cell and lit a great fire and started throwing himself in the fire time after time saying to himself: "If you can't bear the pain of a little fire, how can you bear the torment of the fire of hell?" When the woman saw that she was terrified, took off her expensive raiment, and put on her ragged clothes. Then she came and knelt at his feet begging for his pardon and forgiveness. She promised him that she would spend the rest of her life in repentance. He advised her to join the convent in Bethlehem.

But as for St. Martinianus, fearing the artifices of the enemy of good, he went to an island in the middle of the sea and dwelt there. However, a ship was wrecked nearby the island, and a woman managed to hang on to one of the planks, and the waves washed her to this island. When the Saint saw her, he gave her all what he had of bread. Then he crossed himself with the sign of the cross, and threw himself in the sea, hanging on the wooden plank and he put himself in the hand of the Almighty. The waves threw him on land, and he decided not to settle in one place he wandered about in the mountains and deserts for two years. When he felt that his departure drew near, he went to Athens where he became seriously ill. He asked to see the bishop, and told him all what had happened to him then he gave up his spirit in the hand of the Lord. They shrouded him and buried his pure body with great veneration.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-21.title: The Departure of St. Marcian (Martinianus)

09-22.html:
On this day St. Andronicus departed. This disciple was one of seventy apostles chosen by the Lord who sent them to preach the kingdom of heaven. He was of Jewish origin and was related to the apostle St. Paul. St. Paul mentioned his name in his epistle to the Romans saying: "Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and my fellow prisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me."

The name Andronicus is of Greek origin and means “the victorious man.” He received the Holy Spirit in the Upper Room on the Day of Pentecost. He preached the Gospel in many cities along with St. Junia before the conversion of St. Paul. After St. Paul was converted they accompanied him to many places, the most important of which was the city of Rome. They preached there and endured many sufferings and for that reason when St. Paul sent his letter to the Romans, he sent a special salutation to them.

St. John Chrysostom interpreted the sentence “my fellow prisoners” not to mean that they were taken prisoners but rather that they endured what was more cruel than that. They lived as sojourners deprived of their families, endured hunger, with a continuous threat of death and fell into many difficulties.

When they completed their good endeavor and the Lord willed to take them away from this world, St. Andronicus fell ill for a short time, then departed in peace. St. Junia shrouded him and prayed over St. Andronicus and buried him in a cave. St. Junia prayed to the Lord to take him also and he departed on the next day.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-22.title: The Departure of St. Andronicus, one of the Seventy Disciples

09-22.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) was the martyrdom of 142 young men and 28 women from the mothers of these young men who were natives of Assuit. After the martyrdom of the six soldiers who accompanied St. Claudius, Stratelates, the ruler ordered the imprisonment of Claudius, Abamoun and Serna. In prison, they praised God with spiritual songs along with all the other prisoners.

Nearby the place where St. Abamoun was being tormented was a school with a teacher who was Christian. He encouraged the young men to go to the place of torture and confess the name of the Lord Christ before the governor. When the governor saw them, he was amazed and asked them, “Where are your parents?” They answered him, saying, “Our Father is in heaven and our mother is the church.” Claudius saw this scene and he rejoiced and started encouraging the young men. Their teacher sang the psalm, “Praise God, in all His saints,” and the young men replied with a beautiful spiritual voice. This scene excited the multitudes and everyone went around the city declaring what had happened. Twenty-eight women from the mothers of these young men came and asked their children, “What happened to you? Do you want to go to the Lord Christ and leave us alone in this world?” When the governor became enraged by what he had heard and seen, he cast them all into the fiery furnace. Thus, they received the crowns of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-22.title: The martyrdom of 142 Young Men and 28 Women

09-22.html:
On this day also of the year 64 of the martyrs (348 A.D.), the great saint Abba Amoun, the founder of monasticism in the wilderness of Nitria, departed. This Holy Father was born in the year 275 A.D., to a Christian, godly and wealthy family, nearby Mariout west of Alexandria. He lost his parents at a young age so his uncle took care of raising him. When he was twenty-two years old his uncle forced him to marry. He convinced his wife to live a celibate life and she agreed with him. They often spent time in vigils and prayers and lived as such for 18 years. Then they agreed to follow the monastic life. She went to a convent of virgins and he went to mount Nitria (Barnug) where he dedicated himself to asceticism and worship. He was the first one to dwell in this wilderness.

When the account of his holiness became well known, many gathered around him from those desiring the ascetic life and became his disciples. Monastic groups spread in this wilderness. When the monks became many in mount Nitria, Abba Amoun founded the region of el-Qalali (Cellia) for those desiring seclusion and solitary life.

Abba Amoun was known for the virtue of extreme shyness as he was known for the simplicity of his life. He ate a little bread and often times he spent a day or two in strict abstinence. He spent his time in serenity and contemplation in divine matters and instructing the brethren. God granted him the gift of performing miracles.

In the latter part of his life, he visited the saint Abba Antonius who prophesied about him that his departure had drawn near. Shortly after his return to his cell, he reposed in the Lord after a long strife. The Holy Father Abba Antonius, while he was in Mount Araba in the Eastern desert, saw the spirit of the saint Abba Amoun ascending to heaven with the jubilation of the angels and saints. He made it known to those present with him and they glorified God and his saint Abba Amoun.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-22.title: The Departure of St. Amoun, the Founder of the Wilderness of Nitria

09-23.html:
On this day, St. Junia, one of the seventy apostles, departed. They were chosen by the Lord and sent them to preach the kingdom of heaven. He was born in Beit Gibrael from the tribe of Judah. He received the gift of Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost. He preached the Gospel along with St. Andronicus. They were associated with the apostle St. Paul so that when he wrote his epistle to the Romans he sent a special salutation to them.

After the departure of St. Andronicus, St. Junia shrouded and buried him, he prayed to the Lord not to be separated from him, so he also departed in the following day.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-23.title: The Departure of St. Junia, One of the Seventy Apostles

09-23.html:
On this day also of the year 20 of the martyrs (304 A.D.) St. Thecla was martyred during the torment of St. Claudius. During the torture of St. Claudius, Stratelates (Prince) at the hand of Arianus the proconsul of Ansena in the city of Assuit, and while St. Abamoun was on the red hot iron bed, the martyrdom of the six soldiers, the martyrdom of the 142 young men and 28 women from the mothers of these young men, St. Thecla the daughter of Karas, a noble man from the city of Assuit, dressed in splendid garment came to the place of torment. She talked to the saints Claudius and Abamoun as her brothers. The governor became infuriated and ordered her beheaded early in the next morning in the eastern side of Assuit thus she received the crown of martyrdom.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-23.title: The Martyrdom of St. Thecla during the passion of St. Claudius

09-23.html:
Today also of the year 56 of the martyrs (340 A.D.) marks the departure of St. Botamoun the bishop and Confessor. He was a bishop of Heraclia in Egypt. Pope Athanasius the apostolic testified about him saying; “He was twice martyred for he witnessed to the truth against the pagan persecution as he did against the Arian persecution.”

When Maximianus incited the persecution against the Christians in the year 310 A.D., this saint suffered many tortures. During these tortures he lost one of his eyes and he considered it as his honor especially when he attended the council of Nicaea in 325 A.D. In the council he had a vital role against the Arians who denied the divinity of the Lord Christ.

In the year 335 A.D. he attended the council of Tyre where he defended Pope Athanasius as the champion of faith. He blamed bishop Eusebius, who was his fellow prisoner, how could he accept to judge the champion of faith and he previously had cowardly offered a sacrifice to the idols? Therefore he lost the right to preside over the council.

During the days of Constantius, the Arian emperor, the governor of Egypt Philagrius travelled around with Gregory the Arian Patriarch along with the soldiers to different parts of Egypt. They tortured the Orthodox believers and exiled the bishops. One of their victims was St. Botamoun, they seized and beat him with rods until he completely became unconscious and they thought that he was dead. Some believers took the saint and treated him. However not long after he departed as a result of all the tortures that befell him as one of the confessors.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-23.title: The Departure of St. Botamoun the Confessor

09-23.html:
On this day also, St. Julian and his mother were martyred in the city of Alexandria.

The blessing of their prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-23.title: The Martyrdom of St. Julian (Yulianus) and his Mother in Alexandria

09-24.html:
On this day the church celebrates the feast of the entry of our Lord Jesus Christ into the land of Egypt along with His mother the Virgin St. Mary and the righteous St. Joseph.

The angel of the Lord appeared to St. Joseph in a dream, saying: "Arise, take the young Child and His mother, flee to Egypt, and stay there until I bring you word; for Herod will seek the young Child to destroy Him." (Mt. 2:13)

Immediately they left Israel and they must have passed by Al Arish then the city of el-Farma in Sinai. From There they went to Tel Basta nearby Zagazig where the idols fell what angered the Egyptian priests and they mistreated the Holy Family. Nearby they rested under a tree where the Child caused a water spring to well up from the ground and the water of the spring became a cure for all sicknesses. This place was called “el-Mahamma” for the Child Jesus was bathed in its water. The Holy Family stopped at that place on their way back to Palestine.

From el-Mahamma they went to Belbeis and rested under a tree which came to be called “the Virgin Mary’s Tree.” From there the Holy Family went to “Meniet Genah” then to “Samannoud" where they crossed the Nile to the western shore and came to Sakha. There the Child left a print of His foot on a rock and the place was called "Pekha Issous" which means “the heel of Jesus”.

From there, they went westward to Wadi El-Natroun and the place was blessed by the Holy Family and became a blessing to the entire church for the many monasteries built therein. Then they went to the city of Ain Shams and rested in the shade of “the Virgin St. Mary tree”. There, a spring burst forth miraculously; they drank from its waters and used them to wash the garments of the child, and poured the washing water on to the ground and from that spot the Balsam tree (Commiphora tree) blossomed. This area at present time is called El-Matariya.

Afterwards they moved to Babylon in Old Cairo and lived in a cave which is the crypt beneath Abu Serga church (St. Sergius). The governor of the city heard of them so he pursued them to get rid of those caused the idols to fall. They left the place and embarked on a sailing boat nearby El-Maadi and went to El-Bahnasa where they stayed for five days. They went afterwards to Gabal El-Tair west of Samalout.

It was mentioned by Abu el-Makarim, the historian, that while the Holy Family was sailing on the Nile a huge rock was about to fall down from the mountain on the boat of the Family but the Lord Jesus stopped it by the palm of his hand, imprinting a mark of his palm on the rock preventing it from falling down. For this reason the place is commonly known as Gabal Al-Kaf where Queen Helen built a church after the name of the Virgin Lady known as the church of the Lady of El-Kaf.

From there they travelled to El-Ashmonain nearby Mallawy where they stayed there for a short while however the idols fell which angered the priests of the idols. So they left to a village nearby Dairot then to El-Qoussia where they were violently treated and were evicted after its idols fell down. They escaped to Meir then took refuge in Al-Qussqam mount. They dwelt six months and ten days in the place known by Al-Muharraq monastery where the first altar was built on the stone where the Lord Christ used to sit on.

When Herod died, the angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream saying: "Arise, take the young Child and His mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who sought the young Child's life are dead." (Mt. 2:20-21). Therefore, the prophecy of Hosea was fulfilled which says: "... out of Egypt I called My Son." (Hosea 11:1)

On their way back, they stayed in the cave which is the church of Abu-Serga in Old Cairo. Then they came to El-Matariya, El-Mahama and from there to the land of Israel.

Egypt had profited greatly from this blessed visit which caused all her idols to fall fulfilling the prophecy of Isaiah (19:1): "Behold, the Lord rides on a swift cloud, and will come into Egypt, the idols of Egypt will totter at His presence, and the heart of Egypt will melt in its midst." The Lord also blessed Egypt by establishing in it an altar for the Lord in the middle of the land of Egypt which is the antiquated altar of el-Muharraq monastery fulfilling the prophecy of Isaiah saying; “In that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the Lord at its border; and it will be for a sign and for a witness to the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt.” As he also said; “Blessed is Egypt my people.”

The blessing of this glorious feast be with us all. Amen.
09-24.title: The Commemoration of the Entrance of the Lord Christ into Egypt

09-24.html:
On this day also, the prophet Habakkuk departed. He was one of the twelve Minor Prophets from the tribe of Levi. He was a singer using stringed musical instruments as it is indicated in this verse: "The Lord God is my strength; He will make my feet like deer's feet, and He will make me walk on my high hills. To the chief musician. With my stringed instruments. " Habakkuk is a Hebrew word meaning “embracer.”

His prophetic ministry started after the reformation of King Josiah in the year 622 B.C. then in the period between 621 – 600 B.C. during the reign of King Jehoiakim.

Habakkuk was told by God that the Babylonians will be his chastening rod on the nation saying; “Look among the nations and watch, be utterly astounded! For I will work a work in your days which you would not believe, though it were told you. For indeed I am raising up the Chaldeans, a bitter and hasty nation … to possess dwelling places that are not theirs.” Habakkuk acknowledged that the just in any generation shall live by faith (2:4).

He prophesied about the Incarnation of Christ and His birth, saying: “God came from Teman, The Holy One from Mount Paran. His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of His praise.”

After he finished his good strife, he departed in peace. A church after his name was built in Kartsa - El-Behira governorate in Egypt during the reign of the Christian Emperor Anastasius, and was consecrated on the 24th of Pashons in the early part of the 6th century.

The blessing of the prayers of this great prophet be with us all. Amen.
09-24.title: The Departure of Habakkuk the Prophet

09-24.html:
On this day also, of the year 880 of the martyrs (1164 A.D.) the holy monk St. Bashnouna el-Maqari was martyred.

During the fighting between the men of prince Dergham and the men of El-Wazir Shawer during the Fatimid rule, this monk was arrested. He was threatened with death if he did not convert to Islam, but he firmly refused. They burned him alive thus he received the crown of martyrdom. The Christians took his bones and carried them to the church of Abu Serga in Old Cairo and was buried there.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-24.title: The Martyrdom of the Monk St. Bashnouna El-Maqari

09-25.html:
On this day of the year 22 of the martyrs (306 A.D.) St. Colluthus of Antinoe (Ansena), known as Anba Colta the physician, was martyred. He was born in Ansena to God fearing parents. His father Heraclamon was the governor of Antinoe. He entreated the Lord Jesus to give him a son, and God gave him this saint. He taught him the Christian principles and reading so he memorized many of the books and teachings of the church. He was pure and chaste since his youth. His father wanted him to get married, but he refused. However, his sister married Arianus who became the proconsul after her father. When he became old he asked the Emperor to relieve him from the governorship so he handed the position to his son in law for Colta refused the position.

When the Saint's parents departed, he built a hostel for the poor and sojourners. He also studied medicine which he excelled in and treated the sick without charge.

When Diocletian denied the faith, Arianus the governor followed him to keep his position, and started to persecute and torture the Christians. St. Colta rebuked him for forsaking the worship of the true God. Arianus did not want to inflict any harm on him in respect of his sister. Instead he sent him to the governor of El-Bahnasa, where he was imprisoned for three years until his sister mediated for his release.

After the martyrdom of Arianus the governor on the name of the Lord Christ, another governor took over Ansena. When the new governor knew his account summoned and threatened the saint. When he did not pay attention to his threats, the governor became angry and ordered to torment him. The angel of the Lord came, comforted and strengthened the saint and God performed many signs by his hand. When the governor became weary of torturing the saint he ordered him beheaded thus he received the crown of Martyrdom. They shrouded his body and kept him in a place until the end of the era of persecution, when they built a church after his name. Many miracles were manifested from his body.

The saint has an old church hewn out in the eastern mount in Ansena, a church in "Rifa" district of Assiut, and another church in Shandawil el-Balad district of al-Maragha, Sohag governorate. There is a city after his name in Sohag governorate called “Saqultah” which is a Coptic word means “the region of Colta” nearby Akhmim and there is also a village nearby Mallawy after his name called the village of “Abu Colta” close to Epshadat west of Mallawy.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-25.title: The Martyrdom of St. Colluthus of Antinoe (Known as Abu Colta) the Physician

09-25.html:
On this day also of the year 1511 of the martyrs (1795 A.D.) the great archon and the generous philanthropist El-Mo’alem Ibrahim El-Gohari, departed. His father’s name was Yousef who was a tailor in the city of Qalyub. His parents raised him up in godliness and he learned writing and arithmetic in the village school (Kutab), and he excelled in them. He used to transcribe the religious books and brought them to Pope John (Yoannis) XVIII, the 107th patriarch of Alexandria who was pleased with his devotion and piety and the pope blessed him.

He started to work as a scribe for one of the Mamluk princes. The pope mediated for him to El-Mo’alem Rizk, the chief scribe of Ali Beck El-Kebir, and he accepted him as his private scribe. He continued in his position until the end of the rule of Ali Beck. When Mohammed Abu El-Dahab became the ruler of the country, El-Mo’alem Rizk resigned and was replaced by El-Mo’alem Ibrahim. He was promoted until he became the chief scribe of all of Egypt, a position which is equal to prime minister today, during the reign of Ibrahim Beck. This position increased Ibrahim El-Gohari in humility, piety, generosity, and charity. He attracted to him the hearts of all the people. He married a righteous woman who assisted him in his charitable deeds, encouraged him to build and maintain the places of worship. They had a son whose name was Joseph, and a daughter whose name was Demiana.

Ibrahim El-Gohari remained in his position until a coup took place in the government and Hassan Pasha Qubtan came to Egypt, delegated from Istanbul. He fought against Ibrahim Beck and Mourad Beck forced them to flee together with Ibrahim El-Gohari to Upper Egypt. The new Governor Qubtan Pasha plundered the palaces of the princes, sheikhs, and the possessions of El-Mo’alem Ibrahim and his family. He persecuted the Christians (Copts) and robbed their homes.

The governor was called back to Istanbul, and Ibrahim Beck and Mourad Beck returned on August 7, 1791 A.D. along with Ibrahim El-Gohari.

He was loved by everyone, the government officials and the people. The people called Ibrahim El-Gohari the “Sultan of the Copts.” The famous historian El-Jabarti said about him; “He achieved in Egypt from greatness, influence, power and fame more than any of his people before him had achieved. He was the one referred to in any big or small matter. He had made Egypt great by his capabilities which endured for a long time. He was one of the great world statesmen with a great decisive mind. He treated everyone according to his ability, and did things that attracted the hearts and the love of the people to him. In Ramadan, he used to send gifts to prominent and non-prominent Muslims. In his days, many churches and monasteries were built and maintained, and many endowments of the best of lands were given, with the necessary provisions and salaries.

Abba Yousab el-Abah, bishop of Girga and Akhmim said about him: “He loved all people of different religions, in peace with all, filling all the needs of everyone without prejudice.”

Because of his good relationship with the government officials in Egypt and Istanbul, he was able to obtain special decrees for building churches and maintaining them. The most important of them was the decree to build the church of St. Mark in El-Azbakyah. Because of his influential position in the government, and his great favor with the Muslim rulers, he was able to issue regulations (Fatawi) to permit the Copts to rebuild the destroyed churches and monasteries. He also donated many endowments, from his own money, to the churches and monasteries that amounted to 230 endowments as documented in the patriarchate. He also paid attention to transcribing the church books at his own expense and donated them to the churches and monasteries.

Once his brother Girgis complained to him that some young men insulted him in the street. He asked El-Mo’alem Ibrahim to do something about it. He promised him that he will cut their tongues (shut their mouths). The next day Girgis received great respect from the same young men. When he asked his brother, he replied, saying, “I sent to them many gifts and provisions that cut their tongues from the evil words.”

Ibrahim returned home once after the liturgy of the Feast of Resurrection to find that all the lights of the house were off. His wife told him that the wife of one of the Coptic prisoners came to her along with her children and they were in need of clothes and food. She went with her to the wife of El-Mo’alem Fanous who succeeded in gaining the release of the prisoner. El-Mo’alem Ibrahim brought the man, honored him and arranged a job for him. The man refused and told him, “I have a friend who is in need of the job more than me.” El-Mo’alem Ibrahim rejoiced at his nobility and he arranged for jobs for him and also for his friend.

After a life full of glorious deeds, he departed from this world. The prince of the country, Ibrahim Beck, mourned him and participated in his funeral. The funeral eulogy was delivered by Pope Yoannis.

He was buried in a private tomb beside the church of St. George in Old Cairo.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-25.title: The Departure of the Honored Archon El-Mo’alem Ibrahim El-Gohari

09-26.html:
On this day of the year 72 A.D. St. Thomas, one of the twelve apostles, called the Twin, was martyred. He was born in Galilee, and the Lord chose him for the discipleship and he followed Him (Mat. 10:3). He accompanied His teacher, listened to His teachings and witnessed His miracles. He was loyal, sincere, and eager for knowledge. He searched diligently for the truth and was not convinced except after a careful search and examination.

He manifested his faithfulness when the Lord wanted to go to raise Lazarus from the dead and the disciples knew that the Jews determined to kill the Savior. Thomas said to the other disciples, "Let us also go that we may die with Him” (John 11:16). He was also the one who asked the Lord after the supper, saying, “Lord we do not know where You are going and how can we know the way? Jesus said to him, `I am the way, the truth, and the life.’” (John 14:5-6).

When the Lord Christ appeared to the disciples after the Resurrection in the Upper Room of Zion, Thomas was absent. On his return, the disciples told him, “We have seen the Lord.” He said to them, “Unless I see in His hands the print of the nails and put my hand into His side, I will not believe.” After eight days the Lord appeared again to them and said to Thomas, “Reach your finger here and look at My hands; and reach your hand here, and put it into My side. Do not be unbelieving, but believing.” Thomas answered and said to Him: “My Lord and My God!” Jesus said to him, “Thomas because you have seen Me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed” (John 20:19-29).

The Lord showed Himself to Thomas and six other disciples at the Sea of Tiberias (John 21:1). Thomas witnessed also the Ascension of the Savior along with the disciples and returned with them to Jerusalem. He stayed with the disciples until the descent of the Holy Spirit upon them on the Day of Pentecost.

He went to preach the Gospel in Palestine, Iraq, the Arabian countries, and Persia. In Persia he met the three wise men (Magi) and baptized them. They helped him in spreading the Christian faith in their country. Thaddaeus the apostle, who accompanied St. Thomas, by the guidance of the Holy Spirit went to el-Raha where he cured Abgar, king of el-Raha (Edessa), there he preached Christianity and was martyred.

However Thomas went to India and it was said that he sold himself as a slave. He arrived to India in the year 52 A.D. His master presented him as a gift to the king who loved him for his wisdom and chastity. This relationship permitted him to go on missionary journeys around India. After St. Thomas had established many churches, he wanted to go back to visit all the churches that he had established. He saw on the top of one of the mountains a group of angels who told him, “Hurry and kiss the body of the Mother of God who has been carried by the angels.” After he received the blessing of the pure body, the girdle that was around the body fell and he hurried and picked it up, and kissed it glorifying God.

When he arrived to Jerusalem, after his pastoral visits, he asked to visit the tomb where the holy Virgin was buried for Thomas wanted to reveal the greatness of the miracle of the Assumption of her pure body. He pretended that he did not believe that she had died as all humans and asked to see the pure body. When they lifted up the stone they did not find the body which disturbed them all. However, St. Thomas explained to them how he received the blessing of the Virgin and showed them the girdle.

Shortly after, he returned to India and remained there for about twenty years. In about the year 72 A.D., the number of those who believed in Christianity had increased which provoked the pagan priests to stab St. Thomas with spears. They then flayed his skin and tortured him until he delivered up his spirit. The Christians buried his body in the city of “Malabar”, near the city of Madras in India on a mountain called “Thomas Mount.”

St. Thomas is the patron saint of the Indian Orthodox Christians. The Indian Orthodox Church is affiliated with the Syrian Orthodox Church which is in agreement with the Coptic Orthodox Church in faith.

The blessing of the prayers of this great apostle be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-26.title: The Martyrdom of St. Thomas the Apostle

09-27.html:
On this day St. Lazarus, the brother of Mary and Martha, the beloved of the Lord, departed after he had been consecrated a bishop for Cyprus.

After the Lord had raised him from the dead, he followed the disciples since that time. He was present at the coming of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost. Afterward, they ordained him a bishop over Cyprus and he shepherded the flock of Christ with the best of care. He lived for forty years then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-27.title: The Departure of Lazarus the Beloved of the Lord

09-27.html:
On this day also of the year 168 of the martyrs (452 A.D.) was the Departure of St. Thomas the Anchorite in the area of Akhmim. He was born in the village of Shinshif to God loving and pious Christian parents. They raised him up and reared him on the church manners.

The love of God kindled his heart and since he inclined to the life of contemplation he went to Shinshif mount. He started to practice his spiritual exercises and he loved praying and praising with his melodious voice. He was strict in his asceticism until he ate only once a week. He memorized many parts of the Holy Bible fulfilling its commandments, living the Bible with joy. He increased in virtues until the sweet aroma of Christ outpoured from him. Some heard of him and they visited him to receive his blessing. He did not associate with any of the brethren except at the time of prayers. Some of the brethren who dwelt in the nearby mount visited him to participate with him in prayers.

Once while he was praising using the Psalms, he noticed three men in white garments behind him praising along with him with an angelic voice. St. Thomas rejoiced and went on praising with them all night. Later he knew that they were monks from the monastery of Abba Shenouda, the Archimandrite.

Anba Shenouda visited Anba Thomas often and in his last visit, Anba Thomas told him; “This is the last visit, I shall leave you and the Lord informed me that you shall follow me few days later.” Anba Shenouda asked him for a sign. Anba Thomas told him;”The rock that you sat on outside your dwelling at the time that my soul will depart from my body this rock will split in half like a book that you open.”

When the departure of Anba Thomas from this vain world drew near, the Lord of glory appeared to him, comforted, strengthened, and promised him that a church would be built in this place after his name and people from all nations would come for his name would be widespread.” He also told him that after three days he would leave the body and receive the everlasting crown, and then He bid him peace and ascended to heaven. The Holy Father Anba Thomas departed in a good old age.

Anba Shenouda saw that the rock had split in half and he said, “Truly, Shinshif has lost the luminous lamp of the desert.” Anba Shenouda rose and went to the place of Anba Thomas along with Anba Akhnoukh and Anba Yousab. They shrouded St. Thomas, prayed over him and buried him in the same place of his dwelling.

Many signs and wonders were manifested from his body in the church that was built after his name which still exists till present time. The prophecy of the saint about the departure of Anba Shenouda was fulfilled for he departed on the 7th of Epep of the same year.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-27.title: The Departure of St. Thomas the Anchorite of Shinshif Mount

09-27.html:
On this day also of the year 232 of the martyrs (516 A.D.) the Holy Father Pope Yoannis II, 30th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. He became a monk at a young age and exerted himself with many spiritual fights and lived a solitary life. His fame became well known for his godly life and knowledge and was chosen for the Alexandrian See. He was consecrated on the 3rd of Paone, year 221 of the martyrs (505 A.D.)

He wrote many exhortations and homilies. During his days the church was in peace and tranquility which was supported by the reign of the righteous Orthodox Emperor Anastasius. After the enthronement of Pope Yoannis St. Sawirus of Antioch, sent him a letter to congratulate him and to confirm that; "the Lord Christ after the union has one nature with one Will without separation, and he believed in the same faith of Pope Cyril and Pope Dioscorus."

When Pope Yoannis received this letter, he and the bishops of the church rejoiced, and he replied with an epistle testified in it with the oneness of the essence of God, and the trinity of His Persons, and by the incarnation of the eternal Son of God, the Divine and the human natures have become after the hypostatic union one and no longer two natures, without separation, mingling, or confusion. He anathematized those who separate the two natures, those who confuse them and those who said that the suffering crucified Christ, who died on behalf of mankind, was only a man, and those who say that His Divine nature also suffered and died. He emphasized that the Orthodox faith was to profess that God the word suffered in the flesh that He united with.

When Abba Sawirus read his message, he received it with joy, and made it public in all Antioch.

Pope Yoannis continued to take care of his people, guarding them, doing his utmost effort in teaching the people and renovating the churches that were destroyed by the Chalcedonians. He continued as such for 11 years then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-27.title: The Departure of Pope Yoannis II, the 30th Patriarch of Alexandria

09-28.html:
On this day of the year 119 of the martyrs (403 A.D.) the body of St. Epiphanius arrived to the island of Cyprus. The boat that carried his body arrived to Cyprus from Constantinople on the 28th day of Pashons. The priests and people came out carrying crosses, gospels, candles and incense. They carried his pure body while singing praises and hymns until they placed him in the church.

When they started to dig a tomb for him inside the church, two deacons opposed them. They were excommunicated by the saints for their evil conduct. The body remained in the church for four days without a change or stench. He looked as if he was asleep.

The deacon of the saint came near the body and said: "I know of your favor with God, and that you can restrain these evil opponents." He then took an ax and hit the ground with it. The two opposing deacons fell on their faces unconscious immediately, and they were carried to their homes and died on the third day.

The priests anointed the body of the Saint with costly spices and shrouded it with splendid shrouds, placed the body in a marble sarcophagus inside the church. Many miracles and signs were manifested from his body.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-28.title: The Commemoration of the Relocation of the Body of St. Epiphanius, Bishop of Cyprus

09-29.html:
On this day the church celebrates the commemoration of the three major feasts of the Lord: the Annunciation, the Nativity and the Resurrection of the Lord. The rite of the liturgy is prayed in the joyful tune and no strict abstinence or prostrations.

The blessing of our Good Savior be with us all. Amen.
09-29.title: The Commemoration of the Three Major Feasts of the Lord

09-29.html:
On this day of the year 175 of the martyrs (459 A.D.) St. Simon the Stylite, departed. He was born in Antioch about the year 389 A.D. to Christian parents. His father's name was John, and his mother's name was Martha. He had brothers who died young except one who became a monk however he died in an early age.

His father was a poor shepherd and he sent him since he was young to tend to the sheep. He deprived himself from food to offer it to the hungry. When he was 13 years old he was touched by the Beatitudes which he heard in the church and decided to acquire them. He diligently fasted and prayed, spent his nights kneeling and praying and attended the church regularly.

When his father died, he gave all what he had left to the poor. For two years he visited some ascetics nearby him. Then he went to Taladah and joined a monastery there between Antioch and Aleppo (Halab) where he became a monk and remained there for ten years. He gave himself up to austere asceticism that surpassed all the monastic practices of the monastery.

Later on he left the monastery to the mountain where he found a cave dwelt in it for a while then came to Tel-Nasin which was nearby Antioch. He dwelt in a deserted cell for three years. Then he left it to the top of a mount where he built for himself a fence where he fervently prayed contemplating in heaven and nature. When the people found out about his presence they came seeking his prayers. To get away from his visitors, he found a pillar among some ruins and on the top formed a small platform where he stayed, for this reason he was called the Stylite.

One day a stranger visitor came from Rafina, asked him saying;”Everyone insisted that you did not eat or drink, are you a human or an angel.” St. Simon allowed him to come up with a ladder and he touched him and saw all the sores on his legs. The saint assured him that he did eat as all mankind.

Occasionally he exhorted the people that came to him teaching them to disdain the world, asking them to live a virtuous life, to avoid the love of money, lying and swearing. The saint listened to the requests of the people, healed their infirmities, gave them his various advices and resolved their disputes. Then he would dedicate his time and attention to talking with God through his prayers. The people marveled at his brave ascetic life, performing miracles and his advices and teachings.

In spite of all that he did not neglect caring for the church and its affairs, struggling against paganism, Judaism and heresies, writing in that regard to emperors and hierarchs. After persevering for 37 years from his life on the top of the pillar, reaching the age of seventy years he departed in peace. They prayed over him and relocated his body to Antioch.

His body was relocated to Constantinople in the year 471 A.D. Emperor Zeno built a great cathedral in the end of the fifth century in honor of the saint in the place of his asceticism. The place was called “Simon mount” which is Sheik Barakat Mountain in north Syria.

The blessing of the prayers of St. Simon the Stylite be with us all and glory be to our God forever. Amen.
09-29.title: The Departure of St. Simon the Stylite

09-30.html:
On this day the church celebrates the departure of St. Fores (Fournos), one of the seventy disciples who were chosen by the Lord Christ. He ministered for 3 years and after the ascension of the Savior he served along with the pure disciples. He witnessed the coming down of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost. Then he served along with the apostle St. Paul, and carried his epistles to many countries. He taught many of the Jews and Gentiles and baptized them. He suffered many hardships and sorrows then departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
09-30.title: The Departure of St. Fournos (Fores), one of the seventy disciples

09-30.html:
On this day of the year 818 of the martyrs (1102 A.D.) the Holy Father Pope Michael I, 68th Patriarch of Alexandria, departed. He was born in Sakha and was raised on godliness and purity since his young age.

He was knowledgeable in the church books from his youth, and memorized many of them. He longed for the monastic life and became a monk in St. Macarius monastery. Few years later he was ordained a priest then he went to the area of Singar, and shut himself in a cave for about 20 years. He fought an austere spiritual strife until his fame of knowledge and virtues became well known.

He was chosen for the patriarchate and was consecrated on the 12th day of Paope, year 809 of the martyrs (1092 A.D.). He followed an upright, pure and good demeanor. During which he did not own any money. He lived a modest life and spent what was left on feeding the poor and the needy. He paid the taxes for those could not afford to pay it. He renewed the church vessels and its books. He paid a great deal of attention to exhorting and teaching the people.

During the rule of the caliph Al-Musta’ali bi-Allah and his minister el-Afdal tranquility prevailed in Egypt. One year, the annual inundation of the Nile was seriously short what disturbed the people. The caliph decided to send the Pope to Ethiopia to meet its King and negotiate with him the means to raise the water of the Nile. The Pope went to Ethiopia where they received him with great honor. He asked the king to clear the water course of the Nile from all vegetations to raise the level of the Nile. He stayed for few weeks during which he succeeded in establishing the cordial relation between the king and the Caliph. Pope Michael was the first of the Alexandrian Patriarchs to visit Ethiopia.

When the plague epidemic spread the Pope moved among the sick of his people until he himself was stricken with the disease. The illness did not give him but few hours since he departed on the next day to the paradise of joy. He served the apostolic throne for 9 years, 7 months, and 17 days.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all and glory be to our God for ever. Amen.
09-30.title: The Departure of Pope Michael I, the 68th Patriarch of Alexandria

10-01.html:
On this day St. Corpus, one of the seventy apostles who were chosen by the Lord Christ for the ministry, departed. He preached and evangelized in Judea.

After St. Paul had attended the council of Jerusalem and started his second missionary journey in the year 51 A.D. he chose St. Corpus to join him. When St. Paul established the church in Troas he ordained this saint a bishop over it. On St. Paul way back to Jerusalem in the spring of the year 58 A.D. he passed by Troas to visit the church there and be assured of the wellbeing of St. Corpus.

Before the final imprisonment of St. Paul in Rome, he passed by Troas where he left some of his belongings at St. Corpus and he did not have the opportunity to retrieve them. Therefore he wrote later on from Rome in his second epistle to his disciple Timothy saying; “Bring the cloak that I left with Corpus at Troas when you come and the books especially the parchments.” (2Tim. 4:13)

When St. Corpus fulfilled his missionary work, faithfully served and shepherded the flock of Christ with the best of care, he departed in peace.

The blessing of his prayers be with us all. Amen.
10-01.title: The Departure of St. Corpus, One of the Seventy

10-01.html:
Today also of the year 21 of the martyrs (305 A.D.) was the martyrdom of the saint Abu Fam (Bifam or Phoebammon) the soldier. This saint was born in the city of Taha in Upper Egypt to pagan parents. When he was 12 years old his father offered many gifts to the prince to enlist his son in the army. He was promoted in the ranks until became one of the prominent officers in the palace of Abraht (Apheret). He was known for his love for justice and defending the oppressed.

With the guidance of God, he went to a priest who taught him the principles of Christianity then baptized him. When the ship that carried St. Victor Ebn Romanus was on its way to Upper Egypt, he met the Saint Abi Fam and encouraged him for martyrdom. St. Fam refused to raise incense to the idols during a banquet in honor of the emperor. He was at that time about thirty years old.
